title: Emergent Specialization in Populations of Self-Supervised Collaborative Vision Experts Without a Shared Gate or Cross-Agent Gradients
abstract: arXiv:2609.36770v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Can a population of neural networks develop a useful division of labor without a shared gate or gradients between agents? We study a setting where each network has its own weights, trains independently on the same heterogeneous data, and can ask another agent for help through a forward pass. Unlike mixtures of experts, where a jointly trained gate assigns inputs to experts, specialization here must emerge without central control. We test this in a small scale proxy for predictive visual pretraining. Initially identical agents are finetuned on an unlabeled mixture of six visual domains using masked prediction of frozen DINOv3 features. We measure specialization by asking whether the best agent for an input aligns with its latent domain, and utilization by asking whether responsibility is distributed across agents. We progressively remove central control, ending with DISCO (DIStributed COllaboration) where each agent locally selects a help

translated_title: 无共享门控与跨智能体梯度的自监督协作视觉专家群体中的涌现式专业化
translated_abstract: arXiv:2609.36770v1 公告类型：新 摘要：一群神经网络能否在没有共享门控或智能体间梯度的情况下发展出有用的分工？我们研究了一种设置：每个网络拥有自己的权重，在相同的异构数据上独立训练，并可以通过一次前向传播向其他智能体寻求帮助。与混合专家不同——后者依靠联合训练的门控将输入分配给专家——这里的特化必须在没有中央控制的情况下自发涌现。我们在预测性视觉预训练的小规模代理环境中测试了这一想法：最初完全相同的智能体在六个视觉域的无标签混合数据上微调，使用对冻结DINOv3特征的掩码预测任务。我们通过询问某个输入的最佳智能体是否与其潜在数据域对齐来衡量特化程度，通过询问责任是否分布到各个智能体上来衡量利用率。我们逐步移除中央控制，最终提出DISCO（分布式协作），其中每个智能体在局部自行选择求助对象（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出DISCO框架，证明一群各自独立训练、没有共享门控和跨智能体梯度的神经网络，能够通过分布式协作自发涌现出与数据域对齐的分工特化。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces DISCO, demonstrating that a population of independently trained neural networks—without a shared gate or cross-agent gradients—can emergently develop domain-aligned specialization through purely distributed collaboration.
